title: Preventing fly strike in outdoor rabbits
subtitle: The most common cause of sudden death in UK garden rabbits during summer.
excerpt: Fly strike (blowfly myiasis) kills rabbits rapidly. Flies lay eggs in soiled or wet fur, usually around the hindquarters, and the hatched larvae cause tissue damage within 24 hours. A rabbit can go from apparently healthy to dead in under 48 hours. Prevention depends on daily checks, clean conditions, and correct diet to prevent soft caecotropes.
sourceNotes: RWAF, Fly Strike Prevention guide (2023). PDSA factsheet on rabbit fly strike. BSAVA Manual of Rabbit Medicine and Surgery, fly strike section.

glossaryTerms.definition: A soft, grape-like pellet produced in the rabbit's caecum and eaten directly from the anus as part of normal digestion. Distinct from hard droppings. Soft caecotropes not eaten by the rabbit collect around the hindquarters and attract flies.

content.text: The flies responsible for strike in UK rabbits are mainly Lucilia sericata (green bottle) and Calliphora species (blue bottle). They are attracted to the smell of soiled fur, especially
that have not been eaten and have matted into the fur around the tail and vent. The egg-to-larva cycle takes under 12 hours in warm weather.
Check the hindquarters and vent area at least once every day from April through October. Pick the rabbit up and inspect the fur underneath.
Look for soiled fur, any smell of ammonia or decay, or small white rice-grain-sized objects in the fur. These may be fly eggs or early-stage larvae.
If you find eggs or larvae, act immediately. Remove the rabbit from the hutch, clip away soiled fur with scissors, and call a vet. Fly strike is a veterinary emergency.

Rabbits normally eat their caecotropes directly from the anus. If a rabbit is obese and cannot reach its hindquarters, arthritic and uncomfortable twisting, or fed too many pellets and not enough hay, the caecotropes will not be eaten and will mat into the fur. Correct diet is the single most important preventative measure: hay should make up 85 to 90% of the diet. Overweight rabbits should be put on a weight-loss programme before summer.

Rearguard is a licensed preventative treatment for rabbits that works by interrupting the larval life cycle. It is applied to the hindquarters as a liquid and lasts up to 10 weeks. It is a preventative, not a treatment for active strike. Apply in late spring before the fly season begins, particularly for rabbits that are older, overweight, or have a history of soiled hindquarters.
